narrative:
On July 30, 2026, the Karnataka High Court achieved an overall hearing rate of 41.2%, taking up 937 of the 2,274 scheduled cases across 41 judges. This marks a slight decline from July 29, when the court heard 42.2% of its list (1,041 of 2,467), but an improvement over July 28 (39.5%). Overall scheduled case volume continued to contract from earlier in the week, down from 2,972 cases on July 27.

Disposition efficiency varied significantly across hearing stages and case categories. Matters set for Orders led major stage conversions at 50.7% (411 of 811 heard), while Admission stage cases reached 43.1% (141 of 327). Final Hearings converted at 29.8% (148 of 497), maintaining an upward trajectory compared to 23.8% on July 29 and 22.2% on July 28. Writ Petitions (WP) formed the largest share of scheduled matters, with 271 of 849 heard (31.9%). Stronger clearance performance was recorded in Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) at 52.0% (217 of 417), Regular Second Appeals (RSA) at 58.4% (97 of 166), and Contempt of Court Cases (CCC) at 74.7% (59 of 79).

Bench performance highlights revealed notable output across court halls. Justice H.P. Sandesh achieved a 73.1% conversion rate, hearing 57 of 78 scheduled matters. Justice Chillakur Sumalatha cleared 69.2% of listed cases (45 of 65), and Justice Shivashankar Amarannavar converted 67.1% (53 of 79). Managing the day's largest single list, Justice M. Nagaprasanna heard 60 of 201 scheduled matters (29.9%). High conversion was also seen under Justice B.M. Shyam Prasad, who heard 31 of 36 matters (86.1%) on one list, and Justice Pradeep Singh Yerur, who completed 33 of 54 listed cases (61.1%).
